title: DOE eyes new Cebu power plants to address Visayas supply shortage

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Department of Energy (DOE) is looking to new baseload power plants in Cebu to address the Visayas’ electricity supply shortage, with major projects targeted to add capacity beginning in 2028. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the region needs more dependable power generation as rising electricity demand and recurring power plant outages continue to strain supply. One project is a 150-megawatt (MW) coal-fired power plant in Cebu being developed by Therma Visayas, Inc. (TVI), which is targeted to begin commercial operations in 2028.
